Handmaidens
hănd´mād-nz
n. pl. (female servants; in Joel and Acts, recipients of the outpoured Spirit — Hebrew shiphchah; Greek doule)
From hand and maiden — a maid at hand, a female attendant. The Hebrew and Greek words both mean bondwoman: the lowest rank in a household.

Definition · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Handmaidens are bondwomen, the lowest servants of a house, and Scripture puts them at the centre of Pentecost. Peter quotes Joel: “And on my servants and on my handmaidens I will pour out in those days of my Spirit; and they shall prophesy” (Act 2:18). The prophecy names the classes the ancient world had least regard for — menservants and maidservants — and says the Spirit will be poured on them. In the Old Testament they appear as property: at the meeting with Esau, “the handmaidens came near, they and their children, and they bowed themselves” (Gen 33:6), sent first because they were valued least. Ruth, a Moabitess gleaning in a stranger's field, does not presume even to that rank: “Let me find favour in thy sight, my lord; for that thou hast comforted me, and for that thou hast spoken friendly unto thine handmaid, though I be not like unto one of thine handmaidens” (Rut 2:13). And the word is taken up as a title of honour by the mother of the Lord: “Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it unto me according to thy word” (Luk 1:38). Told that she would bear the Son of God, Mary answered by naming herself a bondwoman and consenting to His word.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines a handmaid or handmaiden as a maid that waits at hand; a female servant or attendant.

expand to see more

HANDMAID, HANDMAIDEN, n. A maid that waits at hand; a female servant or attendant.

MAID'EN, n. An unmarried woman, or a young unmarried woman; a virgin.

BOND'WOMAN, n. A woman slave; a female in bondage.

SERV'ANT, n. A person, male or female, that attends another for the purpose of performing menial offices for him.

Key Scripture

Acts 2:18 — "And on my servants and on my handmaidens I will pour out in those days of my Spirit; and they shall prophesy:"

Luke 1:38 — "And Mary said, Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it unto me according to thy word. And the angel departed from her."

Genesis 33:6 — "Then the handmaidens came near, they and their children, and they bowed themselves."

Ruth 2:13 — "Then she said, Let me find favour in thy sight, my lord; for that thou hast comforted me, and for that thou hast spoken friendly unto thine handmaid, though I be not like unto one of thine handmaidens."

Modern Corruption

Acts 2:18 is pressed to overturn the order of the church, and it is equally mishandled by those who quietly pass over the women it names.

expand to see more

Joel's prophecy, quoted by Peter, says the Spirit is poured on servants and handmaidens and that they shall prophesy. It is regularly enlisted to abolish the male eldership, and it does not reach the question. Prophesying is not the pastoral office; Philip's four daughters prophesied, and the same book of Acts and the same apostolic writings appoint elders who are to be the husband of one wife, apt to teach, ruling their own houses well. The Spirit's gifts are distributed to whom He will; the offices of the church are fixed by Christ's appointment, and neither cancels the other.

The opposite mishandling is more common in conservative churches and deserves naming plainly. The text says handmaidens, and it says the Spirit was poured out on them, and Luke records women in the upper room, women at the tomb first, women labouring with Paul in the gospel, and Priscilla instructing Apollos in her home. A congregation that reads Joel 2 and hears only the sons has abbreviated the verse. The order Scripture gives is not a ranking of worth — Mary's be it unto me according to thy word is the finest single act of faith recorded in the Gospels, and it was spoken by a young woman who called herself a bondwoman.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew shiphchah (H8198), a maidservant, bondwoman — Genesis 33:6, Ruth 2:13; Greek doule (G1399), a female bondservant — Acts 2:18, Luke 1:38.

expand to see more

Hebrew shiphchah (H8198) — a maidservant, bondwoman; Genesis 33:6, Ruth 2:13, Joel 2:29.

Hebrew amah (H519) — a handmaid; the word Ruth uses of herself in Ruth 3:9.

Greek doule (G1399) — a female slave; Acts 2:18 and Luke 1:38, the only two occurrences.

Joel 2:29 is the prophecy Peter quotes, naming servants and handmaidens by their lowest social rank.

Mary's reply in Luke 1:38 takes the title as her own before she is told anything further.

Usage

"“On my servants and on my handmaidens I will pour out… of my Spirit”."

"“Behold the handmaid of the Lord” — the title taken willingly."

"“Though I be not like unto one of thine handmaidens” — Ruth claiming nothing."
